## Function Archive Run

Writes .morph/runs/<runId>/ (deck.json, report.json, answers/ committed with Morph-Run trailers; requests/ ignored); append-only.

Behaviour: archiveRun(root, {runId, deck, report, answers?}, env): runId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, else {ok: false, error: "invalid runId: <runId>"}; an answer whose request.customId does not match it → {ok: false, error: "invalid answer id: <customId>"} (the first such, in order). dir = ".morph/runs/<runId>"; an existing root/dir → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> already exists"} (a run id names one run forever). A refusal writes nothing. Else mkdir -p, write <dir>/deck.json = JSON.stringify(deck.cards, null, 2) + "\n" (the Deck File form, a JSON array of cards) and <dir>/report.json = JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + "\n". Then, answers not empty: <dir>/requests/.gitignore = "*\n" and per answer in order <dir>/requests/<customId>.request.json.gz = gzipSync (node:zlib) of JSON.stringify(request, null, 2) + "\n" — the request copies repeat the slices: kept on disk, ignored in any repo, never committed — and, when text is not null, <dir>/answers/<customId>.answer.txt = text exactly; then <dir>/answers/lines.txt = the answers' lines concatenated in order, when any answer has a line. answers absent or [] → no answers/ and no requests/. Then Commit Paths over [<dir>/deck.json, <dir>/report.json, the answer.txt files in order, answers/lines.txt] with subject "morph run <runId>: deck and report" and trailers Morph-Run <runId>, Morph-Cards <deck.cards.length>, Morph-Written, Morph-Failed, Morph-Skipped, Morph-Budget-Exceeded (the number of report.outcomes with that status). → {ok: true, dir, commit: the sha, or null when Commit Paths returned null}. A git failure of the commit (an ignored .morph/ makes git add refuse) → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> written but not committed: <the Error's message>"}; the files stay on disk. saveBatchRecord(root, record) (exported; record {batchId, …}, a Batch Record) writes <root>/.morph/batches/<batchId>.json = JSON.stringify(record, null, 2) + "\n" (mkdir -p; local state, not committed) and returns ".morph/batches/<batchId>.json"; a batchId outside ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → null, nothing written. saveBatchAnswers(root, batchId, answers) (exported; answers {customId, text}[], from Collect Batch): batchId or any customId outside ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → [], nothing written; else per answer in order <root>/.morph/batches/<batchId>/<customId>.md = text exactly (mkdir -p only when there is one; overwriting) → the relative paths in order ([] for no answers). The directory is a stub processor's ANSWERS_DIR: `morph run` on it replays the answers.

Steps:
- reads: Deck
- reads: Run Report
- calls: Commit Paths
- produces: Archive Result

4. given example 1 with answers [{request: {customId: "a.v1", model: null, maxTokens: null, reasoning: null, messages: [{role: "user", content: "Write a."}]}, text: "```ts\nexport const a = 1;\n```\n"}, {request: the same with customId "b.v1" and "Write b.", text: null}]; when archived; then {ok: true, dir: ".morph/runs/r1", commit: HEAD}; answers/a.v1.answer.txt the text byte for byte, no b.v1.answer.txt, no answers/lines.txt; gunzipSync of requests/a.v1.request.json.gz and b.v1.request.json.gz reads JSON.stringify(that request, null, 2) + "\n"; requests/.gitignore "*\n"; the commit lists exactly .morph/runs/r1/deck.json, report.json, answers/a.v1.answer.txt; git status --porcelain empty; the HEAD message as in example 1

6. given example 1 with runId "r6" and answers [{request: the a.v1 request, text: "A", line: "morph run: a.v1 accepted stage 2 probe finish stop chars 1\n"}, {request: the b.v1 request, text: null, line: "morph run: b.v1 corrupt stage 0 finish none chars none\n"}]; when archived; then ok; answers/lines.txt exactly "morph run: a.v1 accepted stage 2 probe finish stop chars 1\nmorph run: b.v1 corrupt stage 0 finish none chars none\n"; the commit lists exactly .morph/runs/r6/deck.json, report.json, answers/a.v1.answer.txt, answers/lines.txt; requests/a.v1.request.json.gz on disk, git check-ignore names it; git status --porcelain empty

Data Deck: The loaded backlog.
Schema:
{
  "cards": "Card[] in file order",
  "externalDependsOn": "string[] — dependsOn names not in the deck"
}

Data Run Report: The summary of one run (its schema and archive layout are runloop's; the file write and commit are P6 git's).
Schema:
{ runId: string, completedAt: number, branch: string, processor: string, generations: number, outcomes: CardOutcome[], usageTotals: { inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, cost: number | null, requests: number }, requests?: RequestUsage[], fault?: string } — fault only when the run stopped on a fault; requests always set by Run Deck (optional for report literals built elsewhere)

Data Archive Result: The archive written and committed, or the refusal.
Schema:
{ ok: true, dir: string, commit: string | null } | { ok: false, error: string }

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

## Function Submit Deck

The first generation of a deck as one batch; its Submitted Batch saved; one Submit Document.

Behaviour: submitDeck(root, deckPath, processor, deps) → Promise<Detached Result>, every refusal before any call. 1. batchConfig(deps.env, processor) (exported): readRegistry; no config with that id → 4 UsageError "processor <id> is not configured" (+ ": " + the messages of the faults keyed "MORPH_PROCESSOR_<id>_…", "; "-joined, when any); type not openrouter or route not batch → 2 RefusalError "processor <id> is not an openrouter processor on route batch". 2. path.resolve(root, deckPath) not a regular file → 4 UsageError "deck file not found: <deckPath>"; Load Deck faults → 2 DeckError "invalid deck: " + each "<key>: <message>", "; "-joined; no cards → 2 RefusalError "deck has no cards". 3. The cards of Layer Generations' first generation, in deck order, each refused with a reason, first match: acceptance null or blank → "no acceptance"; model set and not config.model → "batch runs one model: <customId> pins <model>, the batch is <config.model>"; Compile Card faults → "compile: <the first fault's message>"; else its requests and input digest are kept. No request → 2 RefusalError "nothing to submit: " + each "<customId> <reason>", "; "-joined. 4. Assemble Batch of the requests; transport = deps.transport or realTransport(config.timeoutMs); ONE fetch(url, {method POST, headers, body}), never retried; Read Batch: thrown → 3 RuntimeError "batch submit: transport: <message>"; an error read → "batch submit: <its error>"; no batchId → "batch submit: no batch id". 5. state = {batchId, processor: config.id, model: config.model, customIds: the requests' ids in order, status: the read's (else "unknown"), cost: null, deck: deckPath as given, submittedAt: deps.now() (its only call), cards: the kept cards, inputs: {cardId: its digest}}; deps.saveState(state) → the state path; null → 3 RuntimeError "batch <batchId>: state not saved", a throw → the same + ": <message>". → {code 0, document {batchId, processor, model, customIds, status, deferred: the ids of the later generations in Layer Generations' order, refused: [{customId, reason}] in deck order, state: the path}}. The batch id leaves in the document and the state file only; nothing is committed.

Steps:
- uses: processor
- uses: cards
- uses: compiler
- produces: Submitted Batch
- produces: Submit Document

3. given example 1 with f.json = [x (model "other/m", acceptance "true"), q (no acceptance), k (contextSlice ["docs/missing.md"], "true"), a ("true")], each → out/<id>.ts; then g.json = [x, q]; when submitted; then code 0, the body's requests only a.v1, refused exactly [{customId: "x", reason: "batch runs one model: x pins other/m, the batch is acme/m:batch"}, {customId: "q", reason: "no acceptance"}, {customId: "k", reason: "compile: contextSlice 'docs/missing.md' does not exist"}]; then 2 RefusalError "nothing to submit: x batch runs one model: x pins other/m, the batch is acme/m:batch; q no acceptance" and one call in all

Data Submitted Batch: .morph/batches/<batchId>.json after submit; a Batch Record plus what collect needs; local, uncommitted.
Schema:
{ batchId, processor, model, customIds: string[], status, cost: number | null, deck: string, submittedAt: number, cards: Card[], inputs: Record<string, InputDigest>, collectedAt?: number, files?: string[] }

Data Submit Document: stdout of submit.
Schema:
{ batchId, processor, model, customIds: string[], status, deferred: string[], refused: { customId, reason }[], state: string }

Callee Commit Paths: Stages exactly the given paths and commits them with a subject and trailers; null when nothing changed.
Behaviour: commitPaths(root, paths, subject, trailers, env, force = false): `git add -A -- <paths>` (`git add -A -f -- <paths>` when force); `git diff --cached --name-only -- <paths>` empty → null, no commit. Else `git commit -q -m <subject> -m <trailer block> -- <paths>`, the trailer block being one "<key>: <value>" line per trailer in the given order joined by "\n" (hooks run; nothing is bypassed), so the message is "<subject>\n\n<trailer lines>". Only the paths are committed: a file staged by hand or modified outside them stays as it was. Then commit = `git rev-parse HEAD` (trimmed) and the diffstat from `git show --numstat --format= <commit>`: files = the number of non-empty lines, insertions and deletions the sums of the first two columns ("-" for a binary file counts 0). Returns Commit Info.

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).

## Function Parse Command

argv into one Command or a usage error.

Behaviour: parseCommand(argv) scans argv left to right. A token starting with "--" is a flag: --pretty and --judge take no value; --root, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches, --slice-cap-bytes, --spec, --component, --map, --out, --checks, --batch take the next token whatever it is; any other flag (--x=y too) → "unknown flag: <t>"; a value flag last → "flag <t> needs a value"; a flag twice → "flag <t> given twice", but --component repeats, its values in argv order (the first error by argv wins). Other tokens are words, giving the command: none → "no command (commands: deck check, plan, run, submit, collect)"; "run"; "plan"; "submit"; "collect"; "deck" "check"; a first word scout, primer, review or report → NotYetError "command <word> is not available yet"; "deck" add|status|reset|clear → NotYetError "command deck <w> is not available yet"; else "unknown command: <words, space-joined>". An extra word → "unexpected argument: <first extra>". Then in order: a flag the command does not take → "flag <f> does not apply to <command>", in argv order (deck check: --root, --pretty, --deck, --slice-cap-bytes; run: --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches; plan: --root, --pretty, --spec, --component, --map, --judge, --out, --checks; submit: --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor; collect: --root, --pretty, --batch); plan without --spec → "missing --spec", else plan is done: the plan Command (components [] and map, out null when not given; checks a key only when given); collect without --batch → "missing --batch", a --batch not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--batch must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')", else collect is done; no --deck → "missing --deck"; run or submit without --processor → "missing --processor"; submit is then done; a run --run-id not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--run-id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')"; numbers in the order --slice-cap-bytes (deck check), --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches (run): digits only, ≥ 1 ("<f> must be a positive integer (got '<v>')"), --max-retry-batches ≥ 0 ("must be a non-negative integer"). A failure is {ok: false, error: {error: {code: 4, kind: "UsageError" | "NotYetError", message}}}. Callee Parse Command: argv into one Command or a usage error.
Behaviour: parseCommand(argv) scans argv left to right. A token starting with "--" is a flag: --pretty and --judge take no value; --root, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches, --slice-cap-bytes, --spec, --component, --map, --out, --checks, --batch take the next token whatever it is; any other flag (--x=y too) → "unknown flag: <t>"; a value flag last → "flag <t> needs a value"; a flag twice → "flag <t> given twice", but --component repeats, its values in argv order (the first error by argv wins). Other tokens are words, giving the command: none → "no command (commands: deck check, plan, run, submit, collect)"; "run"; "plan"; "submit"; "collect"; "deck" "check"; a first word scout, primer, review or report → NotYetError "command <word> is not available yet"; "deck" add|status|reset|clear → NotYetError "command deck <w> is not available yet"; else "unknown command: <words, space-joined>". An extra word → "unexpected argument: <first extra>". Then in order: a flag the command does not take → "flag <f> does not apply to <command>", in argv order (deck check: --root, --pretty, --deck, --slice-cap-bytes; run: --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches; plan: --root, --pretty, --spec, --component, --map, --judge, --out, --checks; submit: --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor; collect: --root, --pretty, --batch); plan without --spec → "missing --spec", else plan is done: the plan Command (components [] and map, out null when not given; checks a key only when given); collect without --batch → "missing --batch", a --batch not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--batch must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')", else collect is done; no --deck → "missing --deck"; run or submit without --processor → "missing --processor"; submit is then done; a run --run-id not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--run-id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')"; numbers in the order --slice-cap-bytes (deck check), --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches (run): digits only, ≥ 1 ("<f> must be a positive integer (got '<v>')"), --max-retry-batches ≥ 0 ("must be a non-negative integer"). A failure is {ok: false, error: {error: {code: 4, kind: "UsageError" | "NotYetError", message}}}. Defaults: root ".", pretty false, sliceCapBytes 500000, runId null, deadlineSeconds 2400, maxCards null (the card count), maxRetryBatches 2.

Callee Deck Check: `morph deck check`: generations, hazards, slice weights.
Behaviour: deckCheckCommand(root, deckPath, sliceCapBytes): Read Deck File (its failure is the result); weighing = Weigh Slices(deck, root, sliceCapBytes); hazards = Find Hazards(deck), then the weighing's; document {deck: deckPath as given, cards: the count, generations: Layer Generations(deck), errors and warnings: the hazards of each severity counted, hazards, weights: the weighing's}, keys in that order; code 2 when errors > 0, else 0.

Callee Plan Command: `morph plan --spec`: record and map cut by Plan Spec, the deck to --out; one Plan Document.
Behaviour: planCommand(root, args), in order. The spec (path.resolve(root, args.spec)) not a regular file → 4 UsageError "spec file not found: <spec as given>"; a given map not a regular file → 4 UsageError "map file not found: <map as given>". loadContour(the spec's UTF-8 text, args.spec), then loadMap(the map's text, args.map) when given (else the empty map {version: 1, package: null, language: null, docs: [], groups: [], cards: [], extraCards: []}); an error → 2 DeckError, it. Plan Spec({record, map, spec: args.spec, components: args.components, judge: args.judge, hasFile: a path is a regular file under root}); an error → 2 DeckError, it. With args.checks: Read Plan Checks (a failure is the result); Build Acceptances({cards, checks, profile: resolveProfile(null, map.language), texts}), errors → 2 DeckError "acceptances not built (<n> error|errors):\n" + them "\n"-joined; its cards replace the plan's, except a card the map gives an acceptance (map card by customId ?? id, extra card by customId). args.out not null → the cards written to path.resolve(root, args.out) as JSON.stringify(cards, null, 2) + "\n", parents created. → {code: 0, document: {spec, components, cards, generations, externalDependsOn, out: args.out}}. Nothing else written; nothing on an error.

Callee Run Command: `morph run`: processor, deck, hazards, run branch, Run Deck, archive; one Run Document.
Behaviour: runCommand(root, args, deps, log?), every check before any git call or spend, in order. 1. readRegistry(deps.env); no config with id args.processor → 4 UsageError "processor <id> is not configured" + (": " + the messages of the faults keyed "MORPH_PROCESSOR_<id>_…", "; "-joined, when any). 2. Read Deck File (its failure is the result); no cards → 2 RefusalError "deck has no cards". 3. Find Hazards errors → 2 RefusalError "deck has <n> hazard error(s): " + each "<kind> <cards ","-joined>[ <path>]", "; "-joined; then cards whose acceptance is null or blank → 2 RefusalError "deck has <n> card(s) with no acceptance: <ids in deck order, ","-joined>". 4. start = deps.now() (its only call here); runId = args.runId or mintRunId(start) (UTC "YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS"). 5. Open Run Branch(root, runId, deps.env); a refusal → 2 RefusalError, its error. 6. Run Deck, input {root, runId, branch, deck, budget {maxCards: args.maxCards or the card count, maxRetryBatches, deadline: start + deadlineSeconds × 1000}}, deps {config, transport: {...(deps.transport or realTransport(config.timeoutMs)), saveBatch: (record) => git's saveBatchRecord(root, record)}, commit: makeCommitHook(root, config.model, deps.env), now: deps.now, env: deps.env, interrupted: deps.interrupted, onVariant: line = variantLine(record), keep {...record, line}, log given → log(line)}. 7. Archive Run(root, {runId, deck, report, answers: the kept records}, deps.env). → {code: 3 when report.fault is set (the partial report archived), else runExitCode(report, archive), document: {runId, branch, base, report, archive}}. variantLine(r) (exported) = "morph run: <r.request.customId> <verdict> stage <stages>[ <lastStage>] finish <finishReason, or none> chars <text length, or none>\n". The checkout stays on the run branch.

Callee Emit Document: One JSON document + newline on stdout; --pretty indents by 2.
Behaviour: renderDocument(doc, pretty) = JSON.stringify(doc, null, 2 when pretty) + "\n". errorDocument(code, kind, message) = {error: {code, kind, message}}, keys in that order (main writes one per invocation to stdout; the log goes to stderr).

Callee Classify Error: Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 a card not written; 2 a refusal before spend; 3 a fault under way; 4 a usage error.
Behaviour: classifyThrown(e) → {code: 3, document: errorDocument(3, "RuntimeError", e.message for an Error, else String(e))}. runExitCode(report, archive) → 3 when the archive is not ok; else 1 when any outcome is not "written"; else 0. Kinds: UsageError and NotYetError (4), DeckError and RefusalError (2), RuntimeError (3).
